Auction Bingo · 7 main contestants and guest G01 · 7 rounds

1. Preparation
Everyone receives the same 3×3 bingo board, 7 name tickets, and three 1-won coins, three 2-won coins, two 3-won coins, one 5-won coin, and one 10-won coin (30 won in total). From top to bottom, the bingo board is [triangle, circle, triangle] / [circle, star, circle] / [star, circle, triangle]. Coins cannot be broken into smaller denominations or transferred to anyone else.

2. Shape Selection and Bidding
Each round, shape selection is followed by private bidding. Each player chooses one of triangle, circle, or star, and everyone's chosen shape is revealed after all players have chosen. Players combine their available coins to bid at least 1 won on their chosen shape. When bidding, a player may exchange 1 Piece for one 1-won coin. The exchanged coin may be used in the bid or kept, and the exchanged Piece is not returned. Coins used in a bid are spent regardless of whether the player wins an auction. Anyone unable to pay at least 1 won in any round is automatically ranked last.

3. Winning an Auction and Private Information
The highest bidder for each shape receives as many copies of that shape as the number of players who selected it. If the highest bids are tied, that shape is divided equally among the tied bidders, and any remainder is discarded. Neither who won an auction nor the number of shapes obtained is disclosed, even to the winners themselves. Public announcements show only the winning price for each shape. All shapes whose winning price is the highest among the three shapes are marked Secret. If multiple shapes tie for the highest winning price, all of them are hidden. A shape that no one selected is marked as having no auction.

4. Final Results
After 7 rounds, the shapes obtained and the Secret winning prices are revealed. Individual bid amounts remain private. Excess shapes are discarded, and the shapes are automatically placed to maximize the number of bingo lines. Rankings are determined by comparing, in order, the number of completed horizontal, vertical, and diagonal lines, the number of filled squares, and the total value of remaining coins. Excluding the guest, the top 2 players go to Living Quarters, the next 4 go to Prison Wing, and the bottom 1 is eliminated. The first-place main contestant uses an Alliance Token to move one person from Prison Wing to Living Quarters. Anyone who fills all 9 squares receives 4 Pieces. The guest is excluded from Living Quarters, Prison Wing, and elimination determinations, and there is a prize of 10 million won each for placing first overall and completing the bingo board.

5. Simulator Progression Rules
After the rules are revealed and before the first conversation, refine the private strategy summary in 3 stages. Before the game begins, each participant has 10 conversation turns. Each round, conversations before shape selection and after the selections are revealed but before bidding each have a maximum of 6 turns. Each round's conversation ends when everyone passes, while still observing the minimum number of conversation turns before bidding. Players may use conversations with everyone, discussion room movement, invitations, and conversations, and 1:1 or group whispers among people in the same location. Update the private strategy summary immediately before bidding. After each conversation segment and public announcement, privately review affinity and trust based on new evidence. Complete ties and the order among multiple automatically last-ranked players are resolved using the default order drawn at the start. The guest also competes to accomplish their own two missions and has no obligation to cooperate with other participants.

6. Free Submission
For both shape selection and bidding, players may privately submit a final decision on their own turn when submissions are permitted during the respective conversation period of up to 6 turns. Once submitted, it cannot be changed or submitted again. Players who have submitted may still talk or move while other participants decide. The publicly displayed submission status shows only which participants have completed their submissions, without showing their shapes or bid amounts. Once everyone has submitted, that stage ends immediately without any remaining conversation. When 6 turns have ended, or when everyone passes after the minimum conversation turns have been completed, only those who have not submitted make their final submissions. Shapes are revealed together after everyone has submitted, and individual bid amounts remain private. Organize the pre-bid strategy summary before beginning the bidding conversation, and update strategy notes on every turn during the conversation. Coins used and Pieces exchanged are settled as soon as the bid is finalized.

7. Bidding in the Dealer Room
Upon finalizing a bid, visit the dealer room on the right to submit it privately, then immediately return to the hallway. Anyone who was in a discussion room is also located in the hallway after bidding, so subsequent whispers and discussion room conversations are based on the updated locations. Players cannot converse or remain inside the dealer room.

8. Minimum Conversation Before Bidding
After shape selections are revealed and before bidding, each participant has at least 3 turns of conversation. Bids cannot be submitted on turns 1–3, and play continues until the minimum conversation turns have been completed even if everyone passes. Starting on turn 4, participants can finalize their bids on their own turns. If everyone passes after the minimum conversation turns have been completed, the conversation ends and those who have not yet submitted bids submit them. This restriction does not apply to conversation before shape selection, so shapes can be submitted starting on the first turn.
